summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of a new, persistent right frontal-parietal headache that did not respond to usual pain medications and was associated with nystagmus. Given her history of CNS lymphoma, imaging and further workup were warranted. MRI of the head showed a stable left parietal lesion with no new masses or enhancement, but increased mucosal thickening in the right frontal sinus. A lumbar puncture was performed to rule out CNS lymphoma recurrence; initial and culture results showed no white blood cells, microorganisms, or growth, supporting absence of infection or malignant cells. The headache was attributed to sinusitis, and she was started on levofloxacin. She remained neurologically stable, tolerated the procedure well, and was discharged home with outpatient follow-up arranged. Her chronic conditions, including common variable immunodeficiency, diabetes, asthma, and hypothyroidism, were managed without change.
